Alice M.: taking prim for the next 4h. Quick context: there was a transient KV-cache stall earlier, we've got a reduced-capacity canary still running. No live pager on me right now but PID #342 is in monitoring. Leaving a short handoff + runbook pointers so whoever picks up later can jump in. TL;DR: check redis-kv hit-rate, model-worker pool, and rate-limiter tokens.

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: incident 342 -> RESOLVED -> monitoring. Alerts saw p95/p99 latency spikes ~1.2s / 3.6s at ~03:12 UTC for text-gen-hosted. Recent deploy was rolled back; restart of model-worker lowered error rate.

Ben R.: thanks Alice. Who's secondary for the window? Any coverage gaps for APAC users?

Alice M.: Carla S. is secondary until 14:00 UTC. Heads-up: there's a ~20min local gap between 13:50-14:10 UTC where both of us would normally be offline if nobody swaps. I'm around to cover but leaving these notes. @Carla S. can you confirm overlap?

Carla S.: confirmed will be on from 13:30 and can take primary at 14:00. Quick triage checklist I use (short):
1) check Kinesis queue depth / backlog,
2) check KV cache hit-rate (Console -> Redis -> Metrics),
3) curl health endpoints on primary inference nodes,
4) check model-worker logs for OOMs or retry storms,
5) confirm rate-limiter buckets not exhausted.
Runbook reference: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-stall (steps 1-5). Also have the fallback routing playbook: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/fallback-routing.

Ben R.: copy. Any quick commands to restart model workers without killing traffic?

Carla S.: prefer graceful rolling restart on the deployment first:

```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-worker-primary
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-worker -o wide
# if a pod is stuck:
kubectl -n inference logs pod/<pod-name> -c model-worker | tail -n 200
```

Alice M.: if rolling restart doesn't clear the issue, do a canary route to the quantized/smaller variant before mass re-route. You can flip routing in the Console or via CLI: 

```bash
rwctl route set --service text-gen --variant redwood-small-quant --weight 100
```

David T.: heads-up — ticket #CC-901 flagged customer-impact (B2B). They saw 503s during the spike. If you do fallback/reroute, please post ETA + rollback plan in #support and ping the account owner.

Carla S.: :thumbsup: will post to #support. Also KV cache nukes are risky — avoid `FLUSHALL`. Prefer targeted key eviction:

```bash
# list hot keys and delete in batches (example)
redis-cli -h redis-primary -p 6379 --scan | grep "model:kv:hot" | xargs -L 100 redis-cli -h redis-primary -p 6379 del
```

Alice M.: quick dashboard + docs links: Observability -> https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency, Runbooks -> https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks. Escalation steps (pager -> oncall L2 -> infra eng) are in the oncall admin doc. I'll also leave a short note in the incident doc if I escalate.

incident-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation change scheduled at 14:00 UTC. If you update primary/secondary, please update /oncall-admin and the rota so paging is correct.

Carla S.: copy — taking primary at 14:00 and keeping these notes. If anyone wants to shadow or pair for the handoff ping me now. I'll post a short summary in #support when I take over. Closing thread unless new alerts come in. :airplane:
